News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

News.title: Sloppy Springboks still strong enough to pulverise Wales
News.content:
If one image summed up South Africa’s complete control, it was in the 12th minute when Wales had a scrum on their own five-metre line. When the Springbok shove came, the Welsh pack went backwards like they were on roller-skates. The poor Welsh front row are going to have to check under their beds for snarling Springboks props for quite a few sleepless nights to come.

Wales’ best period of the game came just after the Springboks’ fourth try when they had three line-outs and took three tap penalties deep inside the South Africa 22. It amounted to absolutely nothing.

You can point fingers at head coach Steve Tandy’s selections and preparation if you wish, but there was little he could have done to change the result. It was only the manner of their hammering, he could have potentially affected.

Wales are not alone in this. Scotland and England may have posed a few more problems but they were still dispatched with ease. South Africa are truly in a league of their own, although New Zealand’s resurgence under Dave Rennie should at least provide a serious level of competition that the British mainland failed to provide.

In truth the best thing that Tandy could do is burn the tapes and hope that this is consigned to the deepest recesses of their collective memory. Tighthead Dillon Lewis especially may need one of those Men in Black memory wipers.

If you squinted hard enough, there were a couple of positives: the maul defence and high-ball contest. They were at least competitive. Aaron Wainwright had the unenviable job of packing down at the back of a retreating Welsh scrum but did a heroic job in the circumstances. Jac Morgan, too, was bravery personified in attacking the breakdown with the ferocity of the Springboks clean-out operation.

But in the infrequent periods when South Africa got on a roll without knocking on, there was precious little Wales could do to stop the green wave. The first try was a case in point. Emanating from a loose kick from Tomos Williams, full-back Aphelele Fassi broke the first line of Wales’ defence and then they kept coming through Cobus Wiese, Damien de Allende before Jasper Wiese accelerated through Morgan’s tackle and over the line.

News.title: Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham
News.content:
United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

News.title: Russell fighting ‘with one hand behind my back’ as Antonelli takes Belgium GP pole
News.content:
Russell and Mercedes are not clueless about his woes. Russell believes he is losing the bulk of the time on the straights, though Toto Wolff, the team principal, conceded that some time is also being lost in the corners. They are both, however, struggling to explain why he is haemorrhaging time in the flat-out sections of a track that is replete with them. It was the same at Silverstone, when Russell repeatedly bemoaned his power deficit to Antonelli and the other Mercedes-powered cars.

Heading into this weekend, Russell believed that these issues were down to Antonelli’s driving style leading to better battery deployment on the straights. “That’s what we thought coming out of Silverstone. We thought it was in the driving style and technique, but we have finally concluded it’s not. We have changed everything... it’s frustrating,” he said.

“So we keep going through this process of ‘Oh, we think it’s this’. We change it. ‘Oh, it’s not this, maybe it’s the driving style’. I thought it was the driving style. Honestly, I came into this weekend and said on Thursday, ‘I think it’s the driving style’. Changed the driving style, and it’s not the driving style.”

“Anything can happen [in the race]. But as I said, the truth is battling against my team-mate, who is such an incredible driver, doing such a great job at the moment, in the best of times, is a tall order.

Sports.title: Kobbie Mainoo shares same World Cup heartache on England duty as his Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK and Kobbie Mainoo have something unique in common: they were both included in England World Cup squads and did not play a minute.

In England’s “celebratory” squad photo with their bronze medals, Mainoo stood at the back. Perhaps deliberately, he placed himself behind the towering Jarell Quansah and John Stones, two centre-backs.



Mainoo bore the same sullen expression in the United States as when he arrived for Manchester United games in the first half of last season.

His headphones were on, drowning out the noise. Mainoo might have heard the rancour over his continued omissions from across the Atlantic.



Mainoo was to Thomas Tuchel what James Maddison was to Gareth Southgate in Qatar 2022. Populist picks they did not really want to make but were crowdpleasing inclusions that took some of the heat off the England manager.

There may be a ‘United>England’ banner permanently pinned up at Old Trafford but United supporters clearly care about Mainoo’s benchwarming tour of the United States.

It was in the USA three years ago that he asserted himself so impressively in the United midfield he was certain to start the season in the starting XI until a freak ankle injury against Real Madrid in Houston.

Mainoo will be available for two games, at the most, for United this pre-season, but he is assured of a starting status at Hull on August 22 – provided that he has recovered from a “sharp pain in the back”.

Conspiracy theories abounded over that timing. Nicky Butt, in shock-jock form on his podcast again, suggested Mainoo should boycott the third-place match against France.

Mainoo was also coincidentally injured for Ruben Amorim’s final three games as United head coach when he would have been assured of a starting role amid a rare Bruno Fernandes lay-off.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

It is still a stretch to imagine that a 21-year-old would feign injury and skip playing at a World Cup. Trevoh Chalobah’s late cameo in Miami meant Mainoo was the only outfield England player not to appear at the finals.

Mainoo had merited inclusion and was wasted when he was needed, particularly in the knockout ties against Norway and Argentina. Carrick, in 2010, was fortunate to make the 23-man cut.

Carrick was reeling from his worst season with United, bookended by high-profile demotions after costly errors against Burnley and Bayern Munich.

His tame penalty failure at Turf Moor allowed Burnley to mark their top-flight return with an unforgettable victory. Against Bayern in the Champions League quarter-finals, Carrick was feeble for Ivica Olic’s momentum-swinging goal and left Arjen Robben unmarked for the tie-deciding strike.

Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and Gareth Barry were mainstays in Fabio Capello’s midfield 16 years ago. Capello tried to coax Paul Scholes out of international retirement, six years on from his last England appearance.



Scholes declined – something he later said he regretted. Capello even checked in on Carrick’s other United teammate Owen Hargreaves, who had played one minute in 20 months.

Capello reluctantly included Carrick. He was handed the No22 shirt, an indicator Carrick would have more time to spend seeing the lions in South Africa than representing the Three Lions.

That World Cup came in the midst of what Carrick described as a two-year depression. He later admitted he did not want to be involved in the England set-up.



Carrick was 28 at the time and his only England World Cup appearance turned out to be a masterful display against Ecuador in the last 16 in 2006. Mainoo, 21, has time on his side, if not Tuchel.

Competition is intense. Jordan Henderson and his pom-poms should not be accommodated at future England camps but Alex Scott, Adam Wharton and James Garner are technicians who, like Mainoo, make a mockery of Tuchel’s “DNA” drivel.

As much as Mainoo’s demeanor during the World Cup has been reminiscent of his final five months under Amorim, he will be returning to an environment at United where he is valued by the coach, the hierarchy and supporters.

He has started in every game he has been available for under Carrick and United’s two defeats came with Mainoo off the pitch. The inevitable five-year contract marks Mainoo as still the biggest recent investment in the United midfield, despite the arrivals of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Mainoo demonstrated in the second half of last season he can hit the ground running after a prolonged period of watching, rather than playing. Tuchel’s September squad announcement should be revealing.



Less than two months after the 2010 World Cup, Carrick was absent from the England squad for the August friendly with Hungary due to an ankle injury.

The next day, Carrick started for United in the Community Shield against Chelsea at Wembley. Awkwardly, he had to pass Capello after collecting his winner’s medal.

Capello seemed to say, “I thought you were injured” and made a telephone gesture to Carrick, as if to suggest to Carrick he should have called to provide an explanation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Carrick played 80 minutes. Sir Alex Ferguson, with a straight face, still said afterwards he was not sure that Carrick was ready.

Mainoo and Carrick might have something else in common.

Sports.title: ‘Will be stronger for it’ – Man Utd goalie Senne Lammens consoled by veteran Red Devils pal after fatal World Cup error
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED veteran Tom Heaton has reached out to Senne Lammens, tipping the young goalkeeper to bounce back “stronger” from his World Cup heartbreak.

A fatal error from Lammens condemned Belgium to a 2-1 quarter-final defeat against Spain, bringing a premature end to their World Cup campaign.



Bound for extra time, Lammens—who replaced the injured Thibaut Courtois ten minutes earlier—fumbled Pau Cubarsi’s 25-yard shot, teeing up Mikel Merino to roof the rebound and book Spain a semi-final with France.

After Courtois, the Belgian bench and even Arsenal‘s Merino rushed to console a shattered Lammens at the end of his horror World Cup debut in Los Angeles on June 10.



United’s goalkeeping unit has closed ranks around Lammens, and Heaton is confident the ordeal will serve the 24-year-old United No1 well in the future.

Speaking after United’s first preseason defeat in Helsinki, Heaton said: “Yeah, I spoke to him (Lammens). He’s obviously off on a break now, a much-needed break, after a long World Cup.

“It was obviously a challenging moment for him, but I think that’s the life of a goalkeeper.

“As soon as you put the gloves on and go between the sticks, you have to be ready to deal with that. He certainly is.

“I actually think he’ll be stronger for it. His personality is fantastic for a goalkeeper, so no issues there.

“It’s obviously disappointing for him, but as I say, I do honestly think it can help him in the long run.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“It’s certainly tough but his personality is suited for it. He’s very strong mentally and he’ll be absolutely fine.”

After a stellar breakthrough season, Lammens won the hearts of United fans and scooped the Premier League’s Transfer of the Season award.

Despite his limited experience—just 64 games in the Belgian top-flight before moving—he thrived under the pressure of being Old Trafford‘s No1.

Having ousted Altay Bayindir to start 32 league matches, Lammens played a vital role in United’s third-place finish has bought him a vast reserve of goodwill.



Asked if Lammens would be anxious about another slip-up, Heaton shrugged it off: “That can happen at any point.

“Literally every time you cross the foot over the earth, so if that’s your mindset and that’s your outlook, then I’d be more inclined to say it’s more likely to happen.

“It’s accepting the fact that it can happen, but what you want to try and do and go and embrace it?

“I’ve certainly seen that from him as a young goalkeeper coming into Manchester United and dealing with that unbelievably well.

“I highly doubt he’ll be going into it with fear or worrying about what may happen, it’s more about what you want to go and achieve, whilst also accepting if it happens you can deal with it.”



He is currently enjoying some downtime with his family during a mandatory three-week break following his World Cup exit.

SunSport revealed last week that United will support Lammens when he reports to preseason, which should be in time for United’s matches in Sweden against Atletico Madrid and PSG.

Heaton played the opening 45 minutes of United’s 1-0 loss to Wrexham in the Finnish capital, conceding the game’s only goal to former United youth star Sam Smith.

Manager Michael Carrick then overhauled his entire lineup at the break, introducing Radek Vitek for the second half.



Heaton, who is embracing a mentorship role in the dressing room this season, spoke highly of the young goalkeeper.

He said: “Radek’s had a really, really good season last year at Bristol. Delighted for him.

“I do rate him highly. He’s probably ready for the next step up. Whether that’s fighting at the top of the Championship, or maybe getting into the Premier League and keeping that development going really.

“But he’s certainly got an awful lot of potential, real good personality for a goalkeeper. He’s assertive, strong in his mind and that’s held him in good stead over the last couple of years.”

Radek said he would be open to another loan or permanent move this summer. United signed former Leeds No1 Karl Darlow on a free transfer last week and Dermott Mee signed a fresh extension.



Any deal would almost certainly include a substantial sell-on clause and a buy-back option.

Sports.title: Inside Argentina’s crazy rituals as sweets, holy smoke, Messi’s lucky boots and strict chicken ban fuel World Cup dream
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL brings out the strangest habits in fans.

Some have a lucky pair of pants, others need a special spot on the sofa, and others will avoid cracks in the pavement like the plague.



It’s the same for players too.

Argentina are set to take centre-stage in New Jersey at 8pm BST tonight as they bid to win back-to-back World Cups.



While Spain will do all they can to stop the South Americans, Argentina’s crazy rituals and superstitions may have already sealed the victory.

Diego Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ goal in 1986 has been embedded into football history.

Fans have called it plain cheating, others claim it feels more like a divine right where the football script is written by something bigger than them.

BROKEN PROMISES

Prior to the 1986 World Cup, the Argentina players are said to have visited the Shrine of the Virgin of Copacabana in northwest Argentina.

The stars promised to return if they won but they NEVER did.

Argentina went on to lose three finals between 1990 and 2014 and all fingers pointed to the curse.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

It was not until 2022, when Lionel Messi and Co became world champions, that the curse was lifted.

And the Argentines have learnt their lesson.

After 2022, Claudio Chiqui Tapia, president of the Argentine Football Association, took the World Cup trophy to different shrines to give thanks.

Rituals, habits, charms. There are all manner of things that can hold onto good luck and cabala is the umbrella over all of them.

Religion and superstition intertwine and morph into one ‘thing’ that helps calm fans as they wish their team through the tournament.



SWEET DREAMS

Rodrigo De Paul and Leandro Paredes chew 14 sweets in the centre circle before every match.

The cabala – which even featured in an advert for Visa – comes from a childhood memory of De Paul’s grandad walking him home from school or training.

De Paul would be given a few coins from his grandad for sweets.



What he did not know was that his grandad was giving him his bus fare and choosing to walk home alone instead.

LUCKY BOOTS

Ahead of the 2022 World Cup, journalist Walter Queijeiro took Messi’s special boots – El Ultimo Tango or the Last Tango – to be blessed at the revered Basilica de Lujan.

And, of course, Messi asked God for protection.

STAY HOME

Argentina president Javier Milei is set to stay home for the final tonight – just as he has done for the other games.

Milei told AP: “No way. I’m going to keep watching all the games from Olivos (a municipality in eastern Argentina).



“Since it’s cold and I don’t turn on the heat, I wear an oil company-branded jacket.

“The day of the Switzerland game, it made me really hot. I took it off, and they scored a goal against us. I put it back on and never took it off again.”

CAPTION THAT

After Argentina handed England a heartbreaking 2-1 defeat midweek in Atlanta, Messi took to Instagram to share a message with his 514million Instagram followers.



He wrote: “ON TO THE FINALS!!!!! We came back to draw strength to make another great match. Thank you very much to everyone who trusted this group!!! Go Argentina.”

But fans were quick to realise that it is the exact same caption from 2022 as the South Americans made the final after beating Croatia 3-0.

So it may well be that Argentina’s No10 is looking for a copy and paste match from four years ago.

CHICKEN BAN

Carlos Bilardo’s road to the 1986 World Cup title included an unexpected casualty – chicken.

Convinced the bird brought bad luck, Argentina’s eccentric manager strictly banned it from the team menu.



BEST FOOT FORWARD

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni revealed that he always steps onto a playing surface with his right foot first.

Speaking to The Athletic, Scaloni said: “I’ve done it since I began playing football and I’ll never stop doing it.

“It doesn’t matter what the result of the game is.”



HOLY SMOKES

Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez are known within the Argentina camp to burn holy wood from the palo santo tree to energetically cleanse spaces, objects, or people.

They allegedly take the incense all around the hotel to cleanse negative energies and meditate before major matches.

HEARTBREAK HOTEL

During the 2024 Copa America, the Argentina national team utilised the Hilton Short Hills in New Jersey.

The hotel clearly left a lasting impression and perhaps a bit of good luck on La Albiceleste.

And they have chosen the same pad for the final stages of the 2026 World Cup.



Keeping the exact same rooms and routines was the ultimate cabala to keep their winning momentum alive.



BARBER LOYALTY

Emi Martinez debuted a bright blue-and-white flag emblazoned across his head in Qatar in 2022.

It’s one of the most ultra-visible signs of national pride for the knockout stages and in 2024 he did it again in the Copa America.

Now he’s brought it back for the 2026 World Cup as they head into the final for a second year running.

ASADO FOR ALL

The Argentina camp reportedly brought over 2,000lbs of meat to Qatar in 2022 to fuel themselves for the World Cup.

But they were not going to just stick it in the oven.



Instead, asado – a traditional outdoor barbecue – was a piece of home.

Tracking all the way back to Kansas City, the players have organised an asado before every game – complete with music.

THE ENEMY

Some fans use aggressive tactics like the cuernitos “little horns” hand sign to jinx opponents.

Others put a rival’s name in the freezer to “freeze” their performance, but many discourage these negative vibes to avoid bad karma.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick sees ‘positives’ in new Man United midfield partnership after Wrexham defeat in Helsinki friendly
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK again touted Mason Mount as a central midfielder after Manchester United’s 1-0 defeat to Wrexham.

United started their pre-season schedule in Helsinki on Saturday without almost all of their World Cup participants.



New signing Andrey Santos started alongside Mount in midfield and the pair played 45 minutes before Carrick picked an entirely different XI for the second half.

Mount ended last season in a deeper role and has started pre-season there alongside the £50million Santos.



The former Chelsea duo cost a combined £110m but could be behind Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans in United’s midfield pecking order.

United missed out on Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes while a move for Atalanta midfielder Ederson collapsed before they brought in Santos and Tielemans this week.

The club want another midfielder and pressure is likely to mount on director of football Jason Wilcox after Chelsea had a £117m offer for Morgan Rogers accepted by Aston Villa.

“There’s loads of little positives to take from the game,” Carrick told MUTV.

“I thought Andrey and Mason did some really good things and connected really well. I could see some positives there.

“Because it is a week in, those sharp little movements and bright moments that you are looking for, they come as you progress through the weeks of training.



“That is what it is. There were good signs from Andrey on his first one, he’s getting in the rhythm and feel of it again, so it was good to see him in a red shirt.”

The United website billed Santos as a “regular” for Chelsea last term even though he started 25 of their 59 matches.

Santos, 22, is the most defensive-minded of United’s fit contingent of midfield options but was billed as a box-to-box recruit by Wilcox.

United still have five weeks until their opening Premier League fixture away at Hull City and they have five more friendlies to play.

The Wrexham game was arranged primarily for the purposes of match fitness and there was a crowd of 20,000 in the 36,25-capacity Olympic Stadium in the Finnish capital.



“As I said before the game, the boys have only been back together for 10 days or so,” Carrick added.

“It was just about getting through today, looking for some positives, looking for some good things and knowing that it wasn’t going to be perfect. That is only natural for the first one.

“I think the most important thing is that everyone came through it in good shape. No injuries, so we can move on and take the next step next week.”

Sports.title: World Cup 2026 golden boot tiebreakers: What happens if players with most goals are tied?
Sports.content:
THE World Cup is heading for a dramatic finale with Argentina taking on Spain in the blockbuster showpiece on Sunday.

Losing semi-finalists France and England went head-to-head in the third-place play off on Saturday night.



The bronze-medal match could prove pivotal in the race for the golden boot as Kylian Mbappe scored twice in a breathless 6-4 defeat to the Three Lions to take his goal tally to ten.

The Real Madrid forward is now two clear of Lionel Messi at the top of the goalscoring standings.



Messi must find the net twice against Spain to go level with Mbappe.

SunSport brings you all you need to know about the golden boot tiebreakers, should the two superstars finish level on goals scored.



World Cup golden boot tiebreakers: What happens if players with most goals are tied?

The World Cup golden boot goes to the player with the most goals at the tournament.

Should players be tied for goals scored at the end of the global showpiece, the winner is the one with the most assists.

If still tied, the golden boot goes to the player with the fewest minutes played.

After the third-place play-off, Mbappe has played 699 minutes at the tournament.



Before tonight’s final, Messi has played 621.

Sports.title: World Cup stadium fury as Fifa face backlash for selling final PITCH and charging fans £2,240 for tiny piece of turf
Sports.content:
FIFA have come under fire once more as they put tiny pieces of MetLife Stadium’s turf up for sale and charge fans an exorbitant amount.

The home of the New York Giants and New York Jets will host the World Cup final between Argentina and Spain tonight in New Jersey.



And the football governing body began selling small pieces of the pitch online from a whopping £335 to an audacious £2,240.

And according to The Athletic, Fifa stand to generate more than a staggering £8.3m in revenue thanks to that initiative.



That led to a furious response from New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill as state taxpayers have already paid for the field.

Sherill claims a staggering £9.7m has already been splashed in taxes to ensure the pitch would be up to Fifa‘s standard.

Steve Sigmund, a spokesperson for the Governor’s office, told The Athletic: “As the Governor has said, New Jersey paid multiple millions for the total expense for the pitch at MetLife Stadium, so New Jersey taxpayers should share in any proceeds.”

Even New Jersey Assembly Republicans agreed with Sherrill – a Democrat – and Assemblyman Mike Inganamort lashed out at Fifa stating this is the “final insult”

Inganamort said: “Fifa needs to get off our turf, literally. New Jersey taxpayers funded $13m in upgrades to MetLife Stadium, including replacing the artificial turf with grass.

“Additionally, the New Jersey Sports and Exposition Authority holds the stadium’s land lease.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“This is state-owned property. Fifa can’t just sell off the soccer pitch without permission. What is happening is not just a bad deal for the taxpayers of New Jersey, it’s illegal.

“The Sherrill administration must use every tool at their disposal to stop Fifa from selling off our field, including seeking a restraining order.

“It is American-grown grass paid for by the taxpayers of New Jersey and planted at a state-owned complex.

“The sale must follow all the rules and laws that dictate how state surplus property is sold.

“It must benefit New Jersey taxpayers — not Fifa or a host committee that splits resources across New Jersey and New York.



“Fifa’s World Cup was bankrolled by New Jersey taxpayers, and they have walked all over us. This is the final insult. It is time this administration stands up to them.”

Sources close to Fifa and the joint host committee claimed they are only partially responsible

They added the host committee will receive the majority of the proceeds, which will go back into continued investments in the region.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “To clarify, the turf sale initiative is a host city-led initiative, not a Fifa revenue driver as incorrectly reported in recent days.

“Fifa receives a nominal royalty fee (<5 per cent) for use of its IP, but a larger share of the revenue generated by this program goes to the NYNJ Host City Committee.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In addition, only approximately five yards of turf will be utilised for this program. Claims that Fifa stands to generate $11m in revenue are categorically false.”

Fifa and its president Gianni Infantino have received intense criticism throughout the World Cup stemming from high ticket prices, Iran’s treatment by US authorities, key figures like referee Omar Artan being denied visas and USA star Folarin Balogun’s red card being lifted.

Sports.title: Argentina stars taunted England from team bus after World Cup win as cutting message revealed
Sports.content:
Argentina stars taunted England from team bus after World Cup win as cutting message revealed

A fresh chapter was added to Argentina and England's long-established rivalry at the World Cup this week

View 3 Images Michael Owen knows all too well about Argentina heartbreak (Image: Arnold Slater /Daily Mirror/Mirrorpix via Getty Images)

Argentina players taunted the England team bus after their World Cup 1998 penalty shoot-out win with blaring music and partying. Alan Shearer made a damning statement to the younger players, including Michael Owen, urging them to "remember this moment" and exact revenge.

‌



The South American side edged further ahead in their rivalry with the Three Lions during this year's tournament, producing yet another late comeback to win 2-1 and advance to the World Cup final. Anthony Gordon's goal had his team 1-0 up but two assists from Lionel Messi helped his side break English hearts once more.

‌



There was a sense of retribution on the cards while England were leading, given their history with Argentina. In 1998, the South Americans dumped Glenn Hoddle's Three Lions out on penalties following a 2-2 draw and David Beckham's infamous red card.

‌



Gabriel Batistuta put away a penalty early on before Shearer levelled with a spot kick of his own. Owen went on a mazy run just six minutes later and fired England in front with a brilliant individual goal, before Javier Zanetti equalised just before half-time.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

England dressing room was left raging after star swapped shirts with Argentina rival READ MORE :

Argentina beat England 4-3 on penalties and Owen was left devastated. Speaking to the Mail before the semi-final, the ex-Liverpool star admitted their rivals spent plenty of time taunting them before leaving the stadium.

‌



Owen said: "We were on the team bus after the game and were underneath the stadium in Saint-Etienne. We’d lost on penalties in the last 16. The bus was quiet and we were all feeling pretty sorry for ourselves.

"There was silence and dejection, a feeling of what might have been. We should have won that night. We looked out of the window and the Argentina bus was parked in the bay next to us.

View 3 Images The Three Lions were left devastated (Image: Stewart Kendall/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

‌



"Their players were just getting on and the party soon started. The music was blasting and, literally, the bus was shaking. Javier Zanetti. Diego Simeone. Gabriel Batistuta. They were banging on the windows and loving every minute of it."

Despite this frustration building among the England stars, Shearer was quick to remind them of the future with a cutting remark. Owen explained: "But I’ll never forget Alan Shearer walking on our bus. He stopped and pointed to the Argentina bus.

"He stood there and at the top of his voice told us, 'Some of you will be lucky enough to play that mob again. Just remember this, remember this moment.'"

‌



View 3 Images Alan Shearer made a strong statement post-match (Image: Bob Thomas Sports Photography via Getty Images)

Four years later, they would indeed meet once more in the World Cup 2002 group stages. Beckham put away a penalty to win the game 1-0 and exact some revenge.

Argentina got the most recent say in the rivalry, however, as they stopped England from making their first World Cup final since 1966.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers' three reasons for choosing £117m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal snubbed
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers' three reasons for choosing £117m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal snubbed

Aston Villa and England star Morgan Rogers is set to snub Arsenal and join Chelsea in a £117million deal after being left highly impressed with the offer from Stamford Bridge

View 2 Images Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea are closing in on a deal to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, with three crucial reasons seeing them beat Arsenal to his signature. News emerged this weekend that Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign the England international this summer, beating the Gunners in the process.

‌



As reported on Saturday, a £117m verbal agreement has been reached between Chelsea and Villa for Rogers to complete a permanent move to Stamford Bridge. The 23-year-old has been heavily linked with a move to Arsenal throughout the summer transfer window, but the Gunners are yet to make an offer in a similar region to Chelsea’s and look set to be beaten by their Premier League rivals to a deal.

‌



Rogers has featured for England at this summer's World Cup, playing his part as the Three Lions reached the semi-final and clinched third place by defeating France. Fresh details have now emerged regarding Rogers' future, providing insight on what Chelsea said to persuade the 23-year-old to put pen to paper with the Blues.

‌



The Athletic have reported that one of the key factors behind Rogers' decision to opt for Chelsea is the vision and long-term project that has been presented to the versatile attacker. Another significant draw is new boss Xabi Alonso, who is currently preparing for his first season as Chelsea boss following his appointment at the start of the month.

Chelsea strike mega £117m Morgan Rogers transfer with Arsenal set to miss out on star READ MORE :

England player ratings vs France as Bukayo Saka and 8/10 stars shine in World Cup thriller READ MORE :

It has also been reported by our sister title football.london that Chelsea have told Rogers they intend to deploy him as a left winger next season, a factor which has further persuaded the World Cup star to make the move to Stamford Bridge. Reports suggest Rogers is set to put pen to paper on a six-year deal to become a Chelsea player, with the contract potentially including the option of an additional 12 months.

Rogers is expected to undergo a medical ahead of completing his move to Chelsea imminently, with the transfer anticipated to be wrapped up shortly afterwards. Should the deal go through, Chelsea would beat their own club-record transfer fee, eclipsing the £107million shelled out to Benfica for Enzo Fernandez back in 2023.

‌



Alonso faced the media at his inaugural press conference earlier this week, with the new Chelsea manager stating: "The way they have, not so long ago, played and competed on the highest level gave me assurance that the potential of the team was there, because of the quality of the players, because of the quality of the way they have played.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Working under newly-appointed Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is a key factor in Morgan Rogers' decision (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce)

‌



"So now it will be the work to carry on many of the things that they've done and to know that we come in a very competitive level, the Premier League, but that's the challenge.

"But I'm sure that with the commitment of everyone, with, for sure, hard work, that's a must, and with the quality on the decisions that we have to take, for sure, we will be there to enjoy a great season. That's what we want.

"We know that the success is a consequence of the good work, of the quality decisions, of the good culture that we want to build, and that's the beauty of such a complex but nice process with so many people involved.

‌



"Always getting the best of everyone, and everyone is committed with the last goal that is being the best we can and giving our best.

"If we all share, day by day, that feeling, I think that we can be optimistic about the future. Tomorrow we start. Tomorrow is day one. We want to feel it. To feel that this is starting something exciting."

Sports.title: Adrien Rabiot slams France team-mates after 'unacceptable' and 'shameful' England loss
Sports.content:
Adrien Rabiot slams France team-mates after 'unacceptable' and 'shameful' England loss

France were on the wrong end of a 6-4 thriller against England in the World Cup third-place play-off, with Didier Deschamps' side having been 4-0 down at the half-time interval

View 2 Images Adrien Rabiot didn't hold back in a post-match interview (Image: beIN Sports)

France midfielder Adrien Rabiot has hit out at some of his team-mates for their 'shameful' attitude towards their third-place play-off against England. Les Blues were beaten 6-4 in Miami on Saturday but were on course for an historic drubbing when England raced into a 4-0 lead before half-time.

‌



Captain Kylian Mbappe inspired a second-half fightback but England managed to get over the line. It certainly wasn't how France wanted to bow out of the World Cup, especially given that it was manager Didier Deschamps' final game after 14 years in charge.

‌



Deschamps' side were coming off a disappointing 2-0 defeat to Spain in the semi-finals, having been the clear favourites to win the tournament after an impressive start. And against England, Rabiot felt that their performance was 'unacceptable', claiming that the foundations for their display were laid before kick-off.

‌



"We entered this first half in a pretty shameful manner," the AC Milan star told beIN Sports. "I've seen behaviours from certain players that I haven't seen until then, for a match like this.

Get the latest World Cup 2026 news in your inbox with our Make Football Great Again newsletter

OPINION England give Thomas Tuchel exactly what he needed with crazy France win in World Cup finale by John Cross

‌



"It's true that it can be disappointing because it's the last match. We had to make a good impact in this competition. It's true that there is a lot of disappointment after the lost semi-final against Spain. There was a job that we needed to do until the end, we can't afford to botch things like that.

"We collected ourselves at half-time, we talked together and we said that we needed a little more pride, that we needed to show something. It was far better in the second half, but in the first, some behaviours were unacceptable."

"We need to emphasise the coach and the staff tonight. They did an excellent job. That's the thing we need to remember. He spoke up in the locker room and thanked everybody. I think we are the ones who need to thank him. We will remember it. We are grateful."

‌



How do you rate France's performance at the World Cup? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images France were beaten in Didier Deschamps's final game as manager (Image: CHANDAN KHANNA/AFP via Getty Images)

Deschamps, who's set to be replaced in the dugout by former France captain Zinedine Zidane, took responsibility for the first half. "It is a defeat, but we were 4-0 down. We produced an unacceptable first half," he admitted.

Article continues below

"There was a reaction, with the things we know how to do well. We had two chances to make it 4-4, but we pushed forward a little more. That is what we know how to do, but we didn't do it. ⁠It is my fault because I must not have done what was needed in the first half."

Sports.title: BBC commentator instantly apologises after Danny Murphy outburst in England vs France
Sports.content:
BBC commentator instantly apologises after Danny Murphy outburst in England vs France

The moment occurred live on air during England's World Cup 2026 third‑place match against France in Miami

View 3 Images Danny Murphy issued an on‑air apology after gesture after slamming his microphone into the table

Danny Murphy's live‑on‑air gesture during England's clash with France prompted commentator Steve Wilson to push him into apologising to BBC viewers. Murphy and Wilson were on duty for England's 6-4 win as they secured third place at the 2026 World Cup.

‌



Thomas Tuchel's side played their final match of the tournament after a heartbreaking 2-1 semi‑final defeat to Argentina. The third‑place play‑off - what looked to be a largely redundant fixture that neither side wanted to contest turned into a breathless goalfest.

‌



The Three Lions stormed into a stunning 4-0 half‑time lead, with goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and a first‑half brace from Bukayo Saka. After the break, the Arsenal forward completed his hat‑trick, before Jude Bellingham added a sixth in stoppage time.

‌



Bukayo Saka speechless before walking away from BBC interview over England World Cup remark READ MORE :

Despite a spirited French fightback, England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966. Saka and Bellingham both came close to adding more, only to be denied in quick succession by France goalkeeper Mike Maignan.

That seemed to infuriate Murphy during commentary in the gantry as Wilson described the moment. The former Liverpool and England midfielder Murphy was seen on the edge of his seat reacting to the missed chances, using his microphone as an outlet for frustration by banging it on the table.

3 View 3 Images Danny Murphy could not contain his frustration on commentary 3 View 3 Images Jude Bellingham scored his seventh goal of an incredible World Cup as England beat France (Image: Jared C. Tilton - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Naturally, viewers at home could hear the noise. Commentator Wilson joked: "Danny, people can hear you if you bang your microphone on the table!," before Murphy apologised.

He said: "Sorry, sorry. It was either that or shout really loud."

Following the disappointment of failing to make it to the final, man of the match Saka felt he could have done more to help his country in the tournament. "Of course I'd love to have played a bigger part but it's too late for that," he said.

‌



"I tried to do my talking on the pitch but it's time to move on. Yeah, I'm fit, I'm fit."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The 24‑year‑old entered the tournament as a fitness concern after being pushed to his limit, playing through injury while helping Arsenal win the Premier League. Saka also refused to be drawn into the criticism surrounding the England manager Tuchel, who faced calls to be dismissed after Argentina's late comeback.

‌



He added: "I think it's just part of the game, when you win there will be noise and when you lose, it's about how you react to it and use it as fuel, we finished strong.

"We built and built across the tournament. We had some amazing results and in the end we fell short against Argentina. It hurts a lot to all of us and I'm sure it's the same to the fans back home but we have to hold out head high and focus on the next one."

We have a busy day’s racing on Sunday with action from Newton Abbot and Chantilly, live on Sky Sports Racing...

12.58 Chantilly - Tokaido faces King Of Cloughan and Beibhinn

A classy field of three head to post for this Group Two Prix Robert Papin at Chantilly.

Amy Murphy saddles Tokaido who recorded a third success on his fourth outing when comfortably claiming the Group Three Prix du Bois under Tony Piccone. That was his first try at six-furlongs and his connections are expecting him to handle this step up in class.

Joseph O'Brien is double handed with King Of Cloughan the pick. A son of St Mark's Basilica, he built on his first couple of starts to take the Windsor Castle Stakes at the Royal meeting. Only on top late on, he will appreciate a decent pace here under new rider Pierre-Charles Boudot.

Beibhinn landed a Listowel maiden on her second start before an excellent third in this grade at the Curragh so cannot be discounted.

Francis-Henri Graffard's gelding is unbeaten in all three starts having burst onto the scene at Saint-Cloud back in March. He takes another step up the ladder here but could prove equal to the test and remains a highly promising prospect.

Christopher Ferland's Silius is a solid yardstick who has claimed silver on his last two starts at this level so must be feared if in similar spirits.

Dark Trooper and Familly complete the shortlist.

Lawney Hill's No More No returned from a layoff to make it two wins from two starts over fences and he makes appeal off a three-pound higher mark. Obviously not the easiest to train, he has been given time to recover from that outing.

Sports.title: England claim third at World Cup with win in 10-goal thriller over France
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka’s hat-trick helped England to a remarkable 6-4 bronze medal win over France in Miami to achieve their best World Cup finish since 1966.

England were incredibly 4-0 up at half-time through Declan Rice's opener, Ezri Konsa's header and Saka's double, as Thomas Tuchel's side took advantage of an uninterested France - but they nearly blew their four-goal lead in the second half.

The two-time World Cup winners woke up after half-time to threaten a sensational comeback through Kylian Mbappe's double - which saw him become the World Cup's all-time leading scorer (22 goals) - and substitute Bradley Barcola's strike.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel hits back at the negativity around England following their World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina saying it felt like they had gone out of the group stges without a win...

Michael Olise missed two glorious chances to equalise before Djed Spence won a late penalty from Malo Gusto's challenge, allowing Saka to score from the spot to complete his hat-trick in the 87th minute.

Yet there was still more drama to come as substitute Ousmane Dembele scored a 96th-minute goal to give France hope of avoiding defeat in Didier Deschamps' last game in charge.

But two minutes later, substitute Jude Bellingham struck with the 10th goal of the game to set the record for the most goals by an England player at a major tournament with seven and secure the Three Lions' third-place finish.

Image: Bukayo Saka hit a hat-trick as England beat France to win the World Cup bronze medal

England's goal-laden display and Saka's performance will only add further frustration and regret over Wednesday's semi-final loss to Argentina, where the Arsenal winger was an unused substitute and revealed after the win over France that he "would have loved to have played more".

Tuchel's name was booed by England fans before kick-off, but smiles and cheers at full-time will give the German hope he can lead them to glory at their home Euros in 2028, where France are set to be led by Zinedine Zidane.

Asked about the criticism in his post-match press conference, Tuchel said it "felt as if we went out in group stage without a win," before adding: "It is the first medal in 60 years, the best World Cup on foreign soil, so I hope the players can be proud of that in some time."

'The most ridiculous game ever'

Image: England have achieved their best World Cup finish since 1966

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett in Miami:

"Who said these bronze medal matches were a waste of time? That was one of the most ridiculous, exciting, open and thrilling games I can ever remember for an England team.

"Of course, there was a huge sense of unreality about it, with 10 goals in a game that looked dead at half-time when England had a 4-0 lead.

"When France started coming back in the second half, there was panic in the England ranks and a sinking feeling, just three days after the lowest of the lows. But credit England's resilience once more and their sheer guts; they ground this one out when the muscle memory must have been saying terrible things to them.

"Mbappe and Olise were running riot by then. But even those two were eclipsed by Saka.

"The Arsenal man becomes only the fourth Englishman ever to score a World Cup hat-trick, and England scored six! That they conceded four, we can discuss another day. Thomas Tuchel didn't park the bus, and it led to a glorious basketball game.

"It is an extraordinary way for England to end their World Cup, one now with the highest finish since 1966.

"Of course, it will anger many - rightly - that Saka and Marcus Rashford were outstanding against France when they were ignored in the semi-final. Of course, the damnation of Tuchel's tactics when it really mattered still stands.

"But let's just enjoy this one, eh? It was a fantastic, rollercoaster ride, where England just about managed to stay in their seats as we looped-the-loop."

Tuchel explains Saka's Argentina omission as he praises 'special' bronze finish

Image: England collect their bronze medals at the World Cup

England head coach Thomas Tuchel speaking to BBC Sport over Saka's omission in the semi-final loss to Argentina:

"He did everything right. I had just a feeling in the semi-final for Morgan Rogers that he would be involved in something special. That was it. The game itself was so in demand that we were forced into changes because of cramps and the flow of the game.

"Bukayo showed he was a key player; that was never a doubt. I was not even aware he had a hat-trick. I lost the overview of the goalscorers."

On the bronze medal win: "It was like four matches - what happened here. Crazy first half and a turbulent second half. You could see the difference what one day makes.

"We were so, so tired and drained from the last few weeks. Massive compliment and respect for the mentality we showed with all the adversity. Absolutely brilliant.

"I was afraid of the physical demand of the match due to the threat of France. They have far less of a schedule for them; it was less demanding. They had one day more after the semi-final and had less travel distances than us.

"This sums it up for us. We played in the heat in extra time, at altitude. I was worried physically. You can see it in the second half, all the cramps and tiredness.

"But I was never worried about the tiredness. This team has created something special. They showed it again."

Image: Bukayo Saka celebrates scoring his hat-trick

Asked whether he could have played more at the tournament, Bukayo Saka told BBC Sport:

"Of course, I would love to have played more. But of course, it's not the time to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch. It's done now. Move on."

On his fitness: "Yeah, I'm fit. I'm fit."

On the noise around Tuchel: "It's part of the game. When you lose, there's always going to be noise. When you win, there's always going to be noise. It's how you react to it and use it as fuel. Today we had to finish strong."

England assistant Barry's 'emotional' half-time interview

England assistant head coach Anthony Barry speaking to BBC Sport at half-time:

"Have to be honest, there's no frustration [they could not perform like this against Argentina]. I'm a little bit emotional, I can't find the words about how proud I am of those players. We're playing a game with broken hearts, 11 lads with broken hearts.

"I've seen them in the hotel in the last few days with broken hearts. They can build a performance like that by playing through pride for England. The team spirit we've built in the last seven weeks.

"The cynics will say it's too late, but we still play against a world-class opponent and I'm so proud of the boys."

How 10-goal thriller unfolded...

3: ENGLAND GOAL! Rice latches onto a misplaced pass to produce a stunning finish.

18: ENGLAND GOAL! Rice turns provider as his corner is headed in by Konsa

37: ENGLAND GOAL! Saka rebounds home from Rashford's one-on-one chance.

45+2: ENGLAND GOAL! Saka collects Eze's through-ball to fire low into the corner and give England a 4-0 half-time lead.

48: FRANCE GOAL! Mbappe pulls one back with a side-footed finish just minutes into the second half.

54: FRANCE GOAL! Mbappe sets up Barcola, who hammers past Henderson at his near post.

66: FRANCE GOAL! Mbappe becomes the all-time leading World Cup scorer with a brilliant finish after a fine one-two with Olise.

87: ENGLAND GOAL! Saka scores from the spot as he sends the goalkeeper the wrong way.

90+6: FRANCE GOAL! Another twist as Dembele cuts in on his left foot and curls one into the corner.

90+8: ENGLAND GOAL! Bellingham seals the win as he dribbles into the area and rounds the defenders to finish from close range.
